questions.question_text: What are the vertex and $y$-intercept of the graph of $y = |2x - 8|$?

options.why: Sign slip when solving $2x - 8 = 0$: divided $-8$ by $2$ instead of moving it across, giving $x = -4$.
Substituted $x = 0$ but dropped the absolute value bars, reading $2(0) - 8 = -8$ as the $y$-intercept.
Made both slips: solved $2x - 8 = 0$ as $x = -4$ and evaluated $y = 2(0) - 8 = -8$ without the absolute value.

questions.solution_text:
Vertex at $2x - 8 = 0 \implies x = 4$, so vertex is $(4,0)$.
$y$-intercept at $x = 0$: $y = |2(0) - 8| = |-8| = 8$, so $(0,8)$.

questions.question_text: What is the range of the inverted absolute value function $y = -|3x + 9|$?

options.why: Ignored the leading negative sign that reflects the V-shape across the $x$-axis.
Substituted the $y$-intercept value as the maximum instead of the vertex $y$-value $0$.
Confused the domain of all real numbers with the range of the function.

questions.solution_text:
Since $|3x + 9| \ge 0$ with minimum $0$ at $x = -3$:
$y = -|3x + 9| \le 0$
The maximum value is $0$ and the graph opens downwards.
$\text{Range} = (-\infty, 0]$

options.why: Used a gradient of $1$ without checking that the $y$-intercept must be $6$.
Used vertex at $x = -3$ instead of the shown vertex at $x = 3$.
Used slope $3$ instead of calculating the slope $\frac{6-0}{3-0} = 2$ on the left arm.

questions.solution_text:
The vertex is at $(3,0)$ and $y$-intercept is at $(0,6)$.
The gradient of the left arm is $m = \frac{0 - 6}{3 - 0} = -2$, so right arm slope is $+2$.
Right branch for $x \ge 3$: $y = 2(x - 3) = 2x - 6$.
$f(x) = |2x - 6|$

options.why: Assumed slope of $1$ without checking that the $y$-intercept is $4$.
Placed the vertex at $x = 2$ instead of the shown vertex at $x = -2$.
Swapped the slope coefficient and the constant term in the absolute value expression.

questions.solution_text:
Vertex is at $(-2,0)$ and $y$-intercept is at $(0,4)$.
Right arm slope from $(-2,0)$ to $(0,4)$ is $m = \frac{4 - 0}{0 - (-2)} = 2$.
Equation is $f(x) = |2(x - (-2))| = |2x + 4|$.

questions.question_text: What is the axis of symmetry and range of $f(x) = |4x + 12| - 3$?

options.why: Read the horizontal shift straight off the constant $12$ without dividing by the coefficient $4$, giving $x = -12$.
Used the range of $|4x + 12|$ alone and ignored the vertical shift of $-3$, giving a minimum of $0$.
Made both slips: took the shift as $-12$ without dividing by $4$, and ignored the $-3$ vertical shift in the minimum.

questions.solution_text:
Vertex occurs where $4x + 12 = 0 \implies x = -3$.
At $x = -3$, $f(-3) = 0 - 3 = -3$, so vertex is $(-3,-3)$.
Axis of symmetry is $x = -3$.
Since $|4x + 12| \ge 0$, $f(x) \ge -3$.
$\text{Range} = [-3, \infty)$

questions.question_text: Determine the parity of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{|x|}{x^{2} + 1}$.

options.why: Assumed absolute value produces odd parity without testing $f(-x) = -f(x)$.
Failed to recognize that both $|-x| = |x|$ and $(-x)^{2} = x^{2}$ preserve the expression.

options.text: Undefined parity due to absolute value
options.why: Incorrectly assumed functions containing absolute values cannot possess algebraic parity.

questions.solution_text:
Test $f(-x)$:
$f(-x) = \dfrac{|-x|}{(-x)^{2} + 1}$
Since $|-x| = |x|$ and $(-x)^{2} = x^{2}$:
$f(-x) = \dfrac{|x|}{x^{2} + 1} = f(x)$
Since $f(-x) = f(x)$ for all real $x$, the function is even.

questions.question_text: What are the vertex and $y$-intercept of the graph of $y = |2x - 10| + 3$?

options.why: Took the horizontal shift directly from the constant $10$ without dividing by the coefficient of $x$, giving a vertex at $x = 10$.
Substituted $x = 0$ but dropped the absolute value bars, evaluating $-10 + 3 = -7$ as the $y$-intercept.
Made both slips: read the vertex $x$ as the constant $10$, and evaluated $y = 2(0) - 10 + 3 = -7$ without the absolute value.

questions.solution_text:
Set the expression inside the absolute value to zero:
$2x - 10 = 0 \implies 2x = 10 \implies x = 5$
Substitute $x = 5$ into the equation:
$y = |2(5) - 10| + 3 = 0 + 3 = 3$
So the vertex is $(5, 3)$.
Substitute $x = 0$ to find the $y$-intercept:
$y = |2(0) - 10| + 3 = |-10| + 3 = 10 + 3 = 13$
So the $y$-intercept is $(0, 13)$.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the function $f(x) = x + |x|$?

options.why: Swapped the conditions for when $|x| = x$ and when $|x| = -x$.
Assumed $|x| = x$ for negative numbers, ignoring that $|x| = -x$ when $x < 0$.
Subtracted $|x|$ from $x$ instead of adding $|x|$.

questions.solution_text:
For $x \ge 0$: $|x| = x \implies f(x) = x + x = 2x$.
For $x < 0$: $|x| = -x \implies f(x) = x + (-x) = 0$.
Outputs on $x \ge 0$ are $[0, \infty)$, and on $x < 0$ output is $0$.
$\text{Range} = [0, \infty)$

questions.question_text: What is the linear equation of the left arm ($x < 3$) of the graph $y = |3x - 9|$?

options.why: Gave the right arm equation ($x \ge 3$) instead of the left arm.
Negated only the coefficient of $x$ and forgot to negate the constant $-9$.
Changed the sign of the constant term without negating the linear term.

questions.solution_text:
For $x < 3$, $3x - 9 < 0$.
By definition of absolute value:
$y = -(3x - 9) = -3x + 9$
